column1: empathetic§An empathetic interviewer gets the answer a hostile one never will.§**有同感**的采访者能得到敌意采访者永远得不到的回答。
emphatic§The denial was emphatic, repeated, and eventually withdrawn.§否认**斩钉截铁**，反复重申，最终却撤回了。
empiric§An empiric collects cases; a theorist collects reasons.§**经验主义者**收集案例，理论家收集理由。
empirical§Empirical work is slow and settles arguments that talk cannot.§**经验研究**进展缓慢，却能了结空谈解决不了的争论。
emporium§The emporium closed and the building became four small shops.§这家大**商场**关门后，楼里开了四家小店。
emptiness§The emptiness of the hall at nine in the morning was startling.§早上九点大厅的**空荡**令人吃惊。
emulate§Do not emulate a style; emulate the attention behind it.§不要**模仿**风格，要模仿风格背后的用心。
enable§Two extra hours a week enabled the whole project.§每周多出的两小时**成全**了整个项目。
enact§The scene was enacted twice for the benefit of the cameras.§为了拍摄，这场戏**演了两遍**。
enchant§He was enchanted by a language he could not yet read.§他被一种自己还读不懂的语言**迷住**了。
encompass§One sentence encompasses what took her a decade to learn.§一句话**概括**了她花十年才学会的东西。
encore§The encore was the only part anyone remembered.§**返场**表演是唯一被人记住的部分。
encounter§An encounter with a bad teacher can last a lifetime.§**遇上**一位糟糕的老师，影响可能持续一生。
encroach§Deadlines encroach on the thinking time first.§截止日期最先**侵占**的是思考的时间。
encumbrance§The title came with an encumbrance from 1890.§这份产权附带着一项一八九〇年的**负担**。
endemic§Delay is endemic to any process with four approvals.§凡是要过四道审批的流程，拖延都是**常态**。
endorse§She endorsed the check and posted it the same hour.§她在支票上**背书**，当小时就寄了出去。
endorsement§An endorsement from a rival is worth ten from a friend.§来自对手的一句**支持**抵得上朋友的十句。
endure§What he could not endure was the waiting.§他**受不了**的是等待。
enervate§A long committee meeting enervates more than a day's walking.§漫长的委员会会议比走一天路还让人**乏力**。
enforce§Enforce the small rule and the large one takes care of itself.§把小规矩**执行**到位，大规矩自然就守住了。
enfranchise§Enfranchising women took three separate acts of parliament.§**赋予女性选举权**用了三部不同的议会法案。
engage§A good opening engages the reader before it informs her.§好的开头先**吸引读者**，然后才告知她。
enhance§Contrast enhances what is already there; it invents nothing.§对比只是**强化**已有的东西，它不创造任何东西。
enigma§The machine is an enigma even to the people who service it.§这台机器连维修它的人都觉得是个**谜**。
enigmatic§An enigmatic reply is often just an unprepared one.§**高深莫测的**回答往往只是没准备好。
enjoin§The rule enjoins silence and nobody has ever obeyed it.§这条规定**要求保持安静**，却从没人遵守过。
enlighten§Nothing enlightens like being wrong in public once.§没有什么比当众错一次更让人**开窍**。
enormous§The enormous cost was buried in a single line of the budget.§**巨额**费用被埋在预算的一行里。
enrage§What enraged him was the tone, not the refusal.§让他**愤怒**的是语气，而不是拒绝本身。
ensemble§The whole ensemble works because no piece calls attention to itself.§**整套搭配**之所以成立，是因为没有一件单品抢眼。
ensure§To ensure a reply, ask exactly one question.§要**确保**得到回复，就只问一个问题。
entangle§Both parties are entangled in an agreement neither remembers signing.§双方都被一份谁都不记得签过的协议**缠住**了。
entertain§The lecture entertained four hundred people for ninety minutes.§这场讲座让四百人**愉快地度过**了九十分钟。
enthrall§A single long shot enthralls an audience that hates long shots.§一个长镜头**迷住**了本来讨厌长镜头的观众。
enthusiasm§Enthusiasm without method produces a very tidy failure.§有**热情**而无方法，只会造就一次整齐的失败。
enthusiastically§He nodded enthusiastically and understood almost nothing.§他**热情地**点着头，几乎什么也没听懂。
entourage§An entourage of four followed her through the museum.§四人的**随行队伍**跟着她走过博物馆。
entrench§Positions entrench when neither side has to pay for being wrong.§当双方都不必为错误付出代价时，立场就会**固化**。
entrepreneur§The entrepreneur sold the company and bought the building back.§这位**企业家**卖掉公司，又把大楼买了回来。
entrust§He entrusted the only key to a neighbor he barely knew.§他把唯一的钥匙**托付**给一位几乎不认识的邻居。
envelop§Silence enveloped the room before the first note.§第一个音符响起前，寂静**笼罩**了整个房间。
envision§They envisioned a library and built a reading room.§他们**设想**的是一座图书馆，建成的是一间阅览室。
ephemeral§Ephemeral printing — tickets, labels, receipts — tells the best history.§票据、标签、收据这类**易逝**的印刷品，讲述着最好的历史。
epistolary§Their epistolary friendship lasted longer than either marriage.§他们的**书信**友谊比两人的婚姻都长久。
epitome§He is the epitome of the careful reader the book deserves.§他正是这本书应得的那种细心读者的**典范**。
epitomize§The last line epitomizes everything wrong with the method.§最后一行**概括**了这个方法所有的问题。
equanimity§Equanimity under criticism is learned, not inherited.§面对批评的**平静**是学来的，不是天生的。
equitable§An equitable rule is not always an equal one.§**公平的**规则未必是平均的规则。
equivocal§His support was equivocal enough to be denied later.§他的支持**含糊**到日后可以否认。
equivocate§Do not equivocate about a date you can check.§对一个查得到的日期不要**含糊其词**。
eradicate§Eradicating the plant took longer than introducing it.§**根除**这种植物比引入它花的时间长得多。
eradication§Eradication was declared and then quietly revised to control.§先是宣布**根除**，后来又悄悄改成了控制。
eradicative§Eradicative measures were dropped in favor of containment.§**根除**性措施被放弃，改为遏制。
erode§Confidence erodes at the pace of unanswered emails.§信心的**流失**，与未回复邮件的速度同步。
erosion§Erosion here is measured in centimetres a century.§这里的**侵蚀**以每世纪几厘米计。
erratic§His attendance was erratic and his work was not.§他出勤**不稳定**，工作却不然。
erratically§The needle moved erratically and then settled.§指针**乱晃**了一阵，随后稳定下来。
erroneous§An erroneous map is more dangerous than no map.§**错误的**地图比没有地图更危险。
erudite§Erudite does not mean unreadable, though it often does.§**博学**并不意味着难读，尽管常常如此。
erudition§Erudition is what is left when the citations are removed.§把引注去掉之后剩下的，才是**学问**。
escalate§Do not escalate a complaint you have not first explained.§没有先解释清楚的投诉不要**升级**处理。
eschew§She eschews adjectives and the prose is stronger for it.§她**避用**形容词，文字因此更有力。
esoteric§What is esoteric in one decade is the syllabus in the next.§这十年被视为**秘传的**东西，下个十年就是教学大纲。
espouse§He espoused two incompatible positions in the same paragraph.§他在同一段里**支持**了两个互不相容的立场。
essential§Strip it to the essential and the argument gets stronger.§剥到只剩**必要的**部分，论证反而更有力。
establish§It is established that the two letters are by the same hand.§这两封信出自同一人之手，**已成定论**。
